instrument: NOT the generated differential harness, and for a reason one step past unit #31's. `vit test-validate` compares a unit's MAPPED OUTPUTS: this unit assigns nothing in CntrPar or objInst and writes ErrVar only on its two I/O-failure arms, so the comparison set would be nearly empty. And both sides of such a harness would OPEN THE SAME PATH -- the filename is a function of the inputs -- so the second call would overwrite the first and the comparison would be of one program against itself. What is checked here is the unit's actual contract: the bytes of the checkpoint file it writes, and the ErrVar it hands back.
measures: TWO STREAMS. CAN see: every one of the 460,813 bytes of every checkpoint, at the exact offset, with NO exemption -- an unformatted STREAM write emits no record marker, no header and no wall clock, so unlike unit #31 there is no line this instrument declines to compare; the SET of files written, which is how a perturbed filename dies; and ErrVar%aviFAIL and ErrVar%ErrMsg, which reach the driver through avcMSG and are printed on every checkpoint step. CANNOT see: any item whose neighbours hold the same value in every checkpoint -- 96 of the 307 written items are constant and ZERO across the corpus (evidence/WriteRestartFile/layout.txt), and 10 of the unit's 16 declared-unreachable mutants are exactly that; the .TRUE. representation of a default LOGICAL, because both logicals this unit writes are .FALSE. in all 195 checkpoints; a checkpoint index of 0 or 1, which is the only input that separates `I0.0` from `%d`; and a RootName long enough to reach CHARACTER(128)'s truncation. Each is named against the mutant that measures it in mutation/WriteRestartFile.unreachable.json.
